syllabus.scope_note: Finals 242 and 251 cover every chapter, from the principles through estimation, scheduling, stakeholders and change.

style.source: Finals 242 and 251, Midterm 251 (both versions) and the instructor's midterm questions
question_types: Scenario MCQs: which principle, strategy or model applies
Short answers that explain what, how and why (one word is not enough)
Case study (e.g. TechNova): pick estimation, resourcing, scheduling and risk techniques and justify them
COCOMO by hand: effort, development time, productivity, staff
Network diagram and critical path, minimum completion time
Define and compare (Gantt vs burndown, project vs general management)
Near-identical terms used on purpose (project vs product management)
style.note: The instructor skips statistics and history (PMI figures, the Manhattan Project).

chapters.title: Ch 1 · Introduction, value delivery and the 12 principles
Ch 1.3 · Tailoring, models, methods and artifacts
Ch 2 · Organizational context: strategy, structure, culture
Ch 4 · Development approach, agile, Scrum and DevOps

items.name: Tuckman's stages
items.memorize: Forming · storming · norming · performing · adjourning

items.name: Situation → tailoring suggestion
items.memorize: Poor quality → more verification loops · unsure team → more guidance and training · slow approvals → streamline

items.name: Estimation methods: pros and cons
items.memorize: Expert judgment · top-down (quick, early) · bottom-up from the WBS (accurate, slow) · analogy (historical data) · priced to win · algorithmic (LOC, function points) · Wideband Delphi (group consensus)

items.name: Scrum terminology and roles
items.memorize: Sprint 2–4 weeks · team 5–8 · product owner (product-focused) · ScrumMaster (team-focused) · daily scrum · product backlog, sprint backlog · potentially shippable increment · velocity

items.name: WBS: process (activity) vs product (entity), work packages, techniques
items.memorize: Process WBS lists activities (PM) · product WBS lists things (engineering) · work packages: 1–2 people for 1–2 weeks · techniques: top-down, bottom-up, analogy, brainstorming

items.name: Motivation: needs hierarchy and personality types
items.memorize: Needs: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-realization · personality: task-, self- and interaction-oriented (balance them)

items.name: Stakeholder management: identify, understand, analyze, prioritize, engage, monitor
Tailoring: definition and why tailor
items.memorize: Deliberately adapting approach, governance and processes to the environment and the work

items.name: Risk identification techniques
items.memorize: Documentation reviews, information gathering (brainstorming, Delphi, interviews, SWOT), root cause analysis, checklists, assumptions analysis, diagramming (cause-and-effect/fishbone, flowcharts, influence diagrams)

items.name: Critical path: forward and backward pass, project duration
items.memorize: Longest path through the network = minimum completion time

items.name: Centralized vs distributed management and leadership
Function points: count, weight, adjust
items.memorize: Count outputs, inputs, inquiries, files, interfaces · apply simple/average/complex weights (e.g. inputs ×3/×4/×6) · adjust by complexity factor

items.name: Lines of code vs function points
RACI / responsibility assignment matrix and skills matrix
items.memorize: Responsible (does it) · Accountable (one owner) · Consulted · Informed

items.name: Risk register
Process, process model, methodology and its elements
items.memorize: Elements: teams, roles, skills, techniques, activities, process, work products, milestones, standards, quality

items.name: Steps to reach consensus
items.memorize: Pose the problem · solicit options · discuss pros and cons · work toward the most beneficial · confirm agreement

items.name: Outcome, portfolio, program, project, product, value
items.memorize: Portfolio: projects, programs and operations managed as a group · program: related projects managed together for benefits · project: temporary endeavour creating a unique product · outcome: end result, the benefit · value: worth, seen differently by each stakeholder. Watch project vs product management

items.name: Status vs progress vs trend vs forecasting vs variance vs earned value reports
Iterative phases: inception, elaboration, construction, transition
items.memorize: Elaboration is the most critical · evolutionary SDLC suits unclear requirements, new technology, high complexity

items.name: Presenting information: dashboards, information radiators, visual controls
DevOps and DevOps project management best practices
items.memorize: Collaborative culture · MVP mindset · on-time and quality delivery · map dependencies · let tools do the heavy lifting · track deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR

items.name: Quality assurance vs quality control vs testing
items.memorize: QA: prevent defects through the process (SQA group, plan, audits) · QC: monitor results against standards · testing measures quality, it doesn't deliver it

items.name: Product backlog items, states and activities
items.memorize: States: ready for consideration, ready for refinement, ready for implementation · activities: refinement, estimation, creation, prioritization

items.name: Corrective vs adaptive vs perfective maintenance; cost factors
items.memorize: Corrective (fix faults) · adaptive (new environment) · perfective (new requirements) · cost 2–100× development; team stability, contracts, skills, structure

items.name: Project management office (PMO)
Software development processes
items.memorize: Ad hoc (code and fix) · prescriptive: sequential (waterfall), evolutionary (iterative, spiral), unified process · adaptive: lean and agile

items.name: Gantt chart: what it shows, advantages, limitations
items.memorize: Easy to read and change · but vague, doesn't always show dependencies or the effect of early/late starts

items.name: Basic COCOMO equations
items.memorize: E = a(KLOC)^b staff-months · TDEV = c(E)^d months · staff = E / TDEV · productivity = LOC / E

items.name: Three-point (PERT) estimate
items.memorize: E = (O + 4M + P) / 6 · standard deviation = (P − O) / 6

items.name: Commonly used models
items.memorize: Leadership: Situational Leadership II, OSCAR · motivation: hygiene vs motivators, Theory X/Y/Z · change: ADKAR, Kotter 8 steps · complexity: Cynefin, Stacey · team: Tuckman, Drexler/Sibbet · other: conflict, negotiation, Salience

items.name: Waterfall: phases, failure symptoms, when suitable
items.memorize: Suitable: clear stable requirements, proven technology, low complexity, enough time · symptoms: late integration and risk resolution, adversarial stakeholders

items.name: Eight project performance domains
items.memorize: Stakeholders · team · development approach and life cycle · planning · project work · delivery · measurement · uncertainty

items.name: Internal vs external project environment
items.memorize: Internal: process assets, governance documentation, data assets, knowledge, security, culture · external: marketplace, social and cultural, regulatory, commercial databases, academic research, industry standards

items.name: Project success criteria and success factors
items.memorize: On schedule, within budget, to requirements, high quality · factors: executive support, user involvement, experienced PM, clear objectives, minimized scope, standard infrastructure, firm requirements, formal methodology, reliable estimates

items.name: Uncertainty, ambiguity (conceptual vs situational), complexity, volatility
items.memorize: Complexity handling: systems-based (decoupling, simulation), reframing (diversity, balance), process-based (iterate, engage, fail-safe) · volatility: alternatives analysis, reserves

items.name: Power/interest grid, Salience model, knowledge base chart
items.memorize: High power/high interest: manage closely · high power/low interest: keep satisfied · low power/high interest: keep informed · low/low: monitor · Salience: power, urgency, legitimacy (definitive, dominant, dangerous, dependent...)

items.name: Critical chain method and buffers (project, feeder)
items.memorize: Like CPM but resource-aware; project buffer at the end, feeder buffers where chains join

items.name: Known, unknown predictable/unpredictable, unknowable risks
Team models
items.memorize: Business team (most common) · democratic · agile/XP groups · chief programmer (surgical) team · skunk works · large teams (formal hierarchy)

items.name: Scenario: which principle applies?
Group cohesiveness, groupthink and communication
System for value delivery and information flow
items.memorize: Portfolios, programs, projects, products and operations create deliverables → outcomes → benefits → value. Leadership shares strategy down; projects send performance up

items.name: Project life cycle vs SDLC
Predictive vs hybrid vs adaptive approaches
items.memorize: Predictive (waterfall): requirements known up front · hybrid: mix where some parts are uncertain · adaptive (agile): high uncertainty and volatility, 1–2 week iterations

items.name: COCOMO modes and constants
Slack (float)
items.memorize: Slack = LS − ES = LF − EF · critical activities have zero slack

items.name: Twelve project management principles
items.memorize: Stewardship · team · stakeholders · value · systems thinking · leadership · tailoring · quality · complexity · risk · adaptability and resiliency · change

items.name: Project velocity
items.memorize: Velocity = story points completed per iteration (10 stories × 3 points = 30) · predicts future capacity

items.name: Integrated change control and the change control board
items.memorize: Recognize need → submit RFC/ECO → evaluate impact → change report → CCB decides → implement and audit → release

items.name: Explicit vs tacit knowledge
Risk management process
items.memorize: Identification → analysis → planning → monitoring

items.name: Pick the risk response (avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept / exploit, share, enhance)
items.memorize: Avoid: remove the cause or cut scope · transfer: insurance, contracts (fixed price) · mitigate: reduce probability or impact · accept: contingency plan or reserve · exploit · share · enhance

items.name: PM people skills: interpersonal, culture, managing people, leadership
Conflict resolution techniques
items.memorize: Confronting/problem solving (root cause) · compromising · withdrawal/avoidance · smoothing/accommodating · forcing/directing · collaborating

items.name: PERT expected time
items.memorize: Expected = (a + 4m + b) / 6 (a optimistic, m most likely, b pessimistic)

items.name: Stakeholder register and management plan
Four types of dependencies
items.memorize: Mandatory (contract or nature of work) · discretionary (best practice) · external (outside the project) · internal (within the project)

items.name: Leading vs lagging indicators and SMART metrics
items.memorize: Leading: predict (rate of change requests, workload balance) · lagging: measure after the fact · SMART: specific, meaningful, achievable, relevant, timely

items.name: What-if analysis, resource leveling, leads and lags, calendars
Delivery cadence: single, multiple, periodic, continuous delivery
Contingency reserve vs management reserve
items.memorize: Contingency: identified risks (known unknowns), controlled by the PM · management: unknown events, unplanned in-scope work. Budget = cost baseline + management reserve

items.name: People-related management activities
items.memorize: Problem solving, motivating, planning, estimating, controlling, organizing

items.name: Burndown chart (axes: time vs work remaining)
Organizational culture: factors and effects on projects
items.memorize: Factors: technology, environment, location, reward systems, rules, key members · effects: departmental interaction, employee commitment, planning, performance evaluation

items.name: Configuration management (version and change control of SCIs)
Product management vs project management, and product life cycle
items.memorize: Product management spans the whole life cycle (introduction, growth, maturity, decline/retirement) and may start programs or projects at any point

items.name: Probability and impact matrix, prioritization (80/20)
Building trust (vulnerability-based)
Risk mitigation, monitoring and management (RMMM); contingency plans
COCOMO by hand: effort, time, staff, productivity
Checking outcomes for each domain
Migration: flash-cut vs parallel operation, back-out plan, data conversion
Stakeholder engagement levels
items.memorize: Unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading

items.name: Risk management plan contents
items.memorize: Methodology, roles and responsibilities, budget, timing, risk categories, definitions of probability and impact, probability-impact matrix, revised tolerances, reporting formats, tracking

items.name: Risk exposure
items.memorize: RE = probability × size of loss (e.g. 25% × 4 weeks = 1 week)

items.name: Measure vs measurement vs metric; product, process, project metrics
items.memorize: Product metrics (static vs dynamic) · process metrics (private vs public) · project metrics · size-oriented vs function-oriented

items.name: Earned value management
items.memorize: CPI = EV / AC · SPI = EV / PV · CV = EV − AC · SV = EV − PV · credit only for 100% complete tasks

items.name: Team needs pyramid
items.memorize: Trust → managed conflict → commitment → accountability → results

items.name: Team structure by objective
items.memorize: Problem resolution · creative · tactical execution

items.name: High-performing team factors and team culture
items.memorize: Open communication, shared understanding, shared ownership, trust, collaboration, adaptability, resilience, empowerment, recognition

items.name: Project in trouble and recovery steps
items.memorize: Options: cut size, increase productivity, slip the schedule · people, process (miniature milestones) and product (stabilize requirements, trim features) steps

items.name: Risk breakdown structure (RBS)
Network analysis, PDM and precedence tables
Internal vs external stakeholders
Technical vs adaptive leadership
items.memorize: Technical: known means, the leader directs · adaptive: no known solution, the leader frames questions and mobilizes the team

items.name: Risk: uncertain event with a positive or negative effect
Risk monitoring: top 10 list, workarounds, reassessments, audits, miniature milestones
Project vs technical vs business risks
items.memorize: Project: plan, schedule, cost · technical: quality and timeliness of the software · business: viability (market, strategy, sales, management, budget)

items.name: Communication types and push vs pull vs interactive
items.memorize: Internal/external, formal/informal, vertical/horizontal, written/oral, verbal/nonverbal · push (memos, reports), pull (portals), interactive (meetings)

items.name: Ethical and professional responsibility in communication
Real vs artificial deadlines; presenting estimates (± qualifiers, ranges)
Emotional intelligence components and leadership styles
items.memorize: Self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, social skill · styles: autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire, transactional, servant

items.name: Planning domain: scope, WBS, estimates, schedule, budget, procurement
Bid documents: RFI, RFQ, RFP
Technology vs social factors on unsuccessful projects
Software quality: requirements, standards, implicit requirements
What to tailor
items.memorize: Life cycle and development approach · processes (add, modify, remove, blend, align) · engagement (people, empowerment, integration) · tools · methods and artifacts

items.name: Model vs method vs artifact
items.memorize: Model: a thinking strategy · method: a means to an outcome · artifact: a template, document or deliverable

items.name: SQA group responsibilities and SQA plan
Plan-driven vs agile change control
items.memorize: Agile: no CCB; the customer owns product changes, the team owns process changes

items.name: Risk tolerance and risk-averse vs risk-seeking analysts
Functions associated with projects
items.memorize: Oversight and coordination · objectives and feedback · facilitate and support · perform work and contribute insights · apply expertise · business direction · resources and direction · maintain governance

items.name: Commitment (clarity and buy-in) and peer accountability
Agile Manifesto: 4 values and 12 principles
items.memorize: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools · working software over documentation · customer collaboration over contract negotiation · responding to change over following a plan

items.name: Extreme Programming practices
items.memorize: Incremental planning (user stories), small releases, test-driven development, continuous integration, refactoring, pair programming, collective ownership, simple design, on-site customer, sustainable pace

items.name: COCOMO advantages, limitations and intermediate cost drivers
Brooks' law and the Mythical Man-Month
items.memorize: Adding people to a late project makes it later; testing is the most mis-scheduled part

items.name: Risk item checklist categories
items.memorize: Product size, business impact, customer, process, technology, development environment, staff size and experience

items.name: Planning communication and the communication management plan
Strategies for threats vs opportunities
items.memorize: Threats: avoid, escalate, transfer, mitigate, accept · opportunities: exploit, escalate, share, enhance, accept

items.name: Heavyweight project organizations (Skunk Works)
Crashing vs fast-tracking
items.memorize: Crashing: add resources to critical activities (costs more) · fast-tracking: run sequential activities in parallel (more risk and rework)

items.name: What to measure (metric categories)
items.memorize: Deliverables, delivery (WIP, lead time, cycle time), baseline performance, resources, business value (ROI, NPV, cost-benefit), stakeholders (NPS, mood chart, morale, turnover), forecasts

items.name: Functional vs project vs matrix structures (strengths and weaknesses)
items.memorize: Functional: no disruption but silos and slow responses · project: PM has sole authority, fast decisions, but expensive and loyalty to the project · matrix: dynamic and efficient, but two bosses and conflict

items.name: Measurement process, data collection and accuracy
Maintenance and change prediction; complexity and process metrics
Percent complete
items.memorize: Completed effort / total effort (e.g. 660 / 2100 = 31.4%), beware the illusion of progress

items.name: Organizational governance system
Factors for selecting a development approach
items.memorize: Product: innovation, requirements certainty, scope stability, ease of change, delivery options, risk, safety, regulations · project: stakeholders, schedule, funding · organization: structure, culture, capability, team size and location

items.name: Definition of done, quality and suboptimal outcomes
Four-step tailoring process
items.memorize: Select the initial approach · tailor for the organization · tailor for the project (product, team, culture) · implement ongoing improvement

items.name: Staff selection factors and working environment
Think small, process spectrum, say no, MBWA
Five-point probability scale
items.memorize: Highly unlikely < 20% · unlikely 20–40% · about even 40–60% · likely 60–80% · highly likely > 80%

items.name: Residual vs secondary risks; fallback plans
items.memorize: Residual: what remains after the response · secondary: new risks caused by the response

items.name: Project manager responsibilities and competencies
PMI Code of Ethics values
items.memorize: Responsibility, respect, fairness, honesty

items.name: Common methods and artifacts
Strategic management and how projects reflect strategy
PMO forms and models
items.memorize: Forms: supportive (low control), controlling (moderate), directive (high) · models: weather station, control tower, resource pool

items.name: Effort vs duration; labor vs clock time
items.memorize: Duration = effort / people (elapsed working days) · labor time is effort, clock time is calendar time

items.name: Over- vs under-estimation (Parkinson's Law, Student Syndrome)
Code reuse (> 50% modified = new) and agile estimation
Lehman's laws
items.memorize: Continuing change · increasing complexity · large program evolution · organizational stability · conservation of familiarity

items.name: Roll-out: release checklist, training, documentation
Communication paths in a team
items.memorize: Paths = n(n − 1) / 2 (50 people ≈ 1,225) · keep teams under 10, 7 ± 2

items.name: Project management and why organizations use it
items.memorize: Applying knowledge, skills, tools and techniques to project activities to meet requirements

items.name: Advantages of formal project management
items.memorize: Better control of resources, customer relations, shorter development, lower costs, higher quality, higher profit, coordination, morale

items.name: Agile vs waterfall (triple constraint)
items.memorize: Waterfall fixes scope and estimates time and cost; agile fixes time and cost and estimates scope

items.name: Why estimation is hard; target vs committed dates
Cone of uncertainty
items.memorize: Estimates converge toward 1× as the project progresses

items.name: Planning vs estimating vs scheduling vs tracking
Software change strategies
items.memorize: Maintenance · architectural transformation · re-engineering
